passages.scripture: When the day of Pentecost came, they were all together in one place.

lines.text: Pentecost was a Jewish feast held fifty days after the feast of Passover — the name Pentecost means “fiftieth.”
At Pentecost, the Jews thanked God for the harvest of grain.
When the day of Pentecost came, the believers were all together in one place.

passages.scripture: Suddenly a sound like a mighty rushing wind came from heaven and filled the whole house where they were sitting.

lines.text: Suddenly a sound came from heaven.
The sound was like a strong, rushing wind.
The believers were sitting in a house.
The sound filled the whole house.

passages.scripture: They saw tongues like flames of fire that separated and came to rest on each of them.

lines.text: The believers saw what looked like tongues of fire.
A tongue of fire came to rest on each of the believers.

passages.scripture: And they were all filled with the Holy Spirit and began to speak in other tongues as the Spirit enabled them.

lines.text: All the believers were filled with the Holy Spirit.
The word that means “tongue” can also mean “language.”
The believers began to speak in other languages.
The Holy Spirit gave the believers the ability to speak these languages.

passages.scripture: Now there were dwelling in Jerusalem God-fearing Jews from every nation under heaven.

lines.text: To be God-fearing is to deeply respect God, knowing that God punishes sin, and so to carefully avoid sin.
There were God-fearing Jews in Jerusalem.
These Jews had come from every nation under heaven — from nations all over the world.
